test_title: PYST 29: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 21 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true regarding the tenure and independence of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India?

options.text: The other Election Commissioners can only be removed by the CEC, not by the government.
The CEC’s removal requires assent of the Chief Justice of India but not necessarily the Parliament’s approval.
The CEC enjoys a fixed tenure of ten years and cannot be replaced before that term under any circumstances.
The CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge by a two-thirds majority in Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Tenure and Removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):** The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) enjoys a secure position under the Constitution. The **removal process of the CEC is similar to that of a Supreme Court judge**, requiring a **two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament**. This ensures independence and protection from arbitrary removal. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• **Election Commissioners' Removal:** Unlike the CEC, the other Election Commissioners do not have the same protection. They can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC. This highlights the relatively greater autonomy of the CEC. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **CEC’s Removal Assent:** The removal of the CEC does not require the assent of the Chief Justice of India, as it is entirely a parliamentary process under Article 324 of the Constitution. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*</li
